searchText: Shit I think I found a bad bug in the spec that was never tested because we didn't use execution requests <@641548687813902336> <@363800010518822915> Will open a PR that will break every single test with them I assume i can help with the tests if you need it nvm, it´s not so bad if we accept that `state.state_roots` has a different meaning and will not coincide with the `state_root` committed in the beacon block, but this makes the above situation discussed about EIP-4788 much worse. However with the new semantics of `state.state_roots`, the problem above is kinda solved. Because the beacon block root contains a state root to which you can prove something about the state after processing the beacon block of N but not the payload. Let that one be `state`, then `state.state_roots[N-1]` will have the post-state root of processing the full payload. Will add a full description of this issue in the next breakout cc <@935504619554107392> as you guys may be affected do we care more about making the sematics the same as today or do we care more about exposing both state roots? if we wanna make the sametics of `payload.state_root` the same as today, it would be something like the beacon state root after applying the payload in `N-1` but before appyling the beacon block of `N` unless `N-1` is skipped or empty.. then it would be the result of applying the beacon block `N` which seems.. horrible there's no "semanthics the same as today" . If I say the state root means the post state after the CL block, then I broke semantics, if I say the state root means the post state after the payload then I keep the same meaning. The thing is that both are the same today and are different tomorrow. And yes, the state root does make the same meaning of today according to your own wording: it is the post-state of the payload of N-1 before the block of N if N-1 is skipped of empty yes, the state root is still the post state of the payload of N-1 (which is empty) is this right? if `N` is full: should be execution's post state root if `N` is empty: should be consensus's post state root if `N` is skipped: at `N+1` process slot, it should be filled with `N-1`'s state root yes, but the consensus post-state root is also the execution poststate root if N is empty. This is how it would look if we overload the consolidations contracts to onboard builders https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/688075293562503241/1408552963382972416

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: nvm, it´s not so bad if we accept that `state.state_roots` has a different meaning and will not coincide with the `state_root` committed in the beacon block, but this makes the above situation discussed about EIP-4788 much worse. However with the new semantics of `state.state_roots`, the problem above is kinda solved. Because the beacon block root contains a state root to which you can prove something about the state after processing the beacon block of N but not the payload. Let that one be `state`, then `state.state_roots[N-1]` will have the post-state root of processing the full payload. Will add a full description of this issue in the next breakout cc <@935504619554107392> as you guys may be affected

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: do we care more about making the sematics the same as today or do we care more about exposing both state roots?

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: if we wanna make the sametics of `payload.state_root` the same as today, it would be something like the beacon state root after applying the payload in `N-1` but before appyling the beacon block of `N`

excerpts.author: ethdreamer
excerpts.content: unless `N-1` is skipped or empty.. then it would be the result of applying the beacon block `N`

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: there's no "semanthics the same as today" . If I say the state root means the post state after the CL block, then I broke semantics, if I say the state root means the post state after the payload then I keep the same meaning. The thing is that both are the same today and are different tomorrow.

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: And yes, the state root does make the same meaning of today according to your own wording: it is the post-state of the payload of N-1 before the block of N

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: if N-1 is skipped of empty yes, the state root is still the post state of the payload of N-1 (which is empty)

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
is this right?
if `N` is full: should be execution's post state root
if `N` is empty: should be consensus's post state root
if `N` is skipped: at `N+1` process slot, it should be filled with `N-1`'s state root

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yes, but the consensus post-state root is also the execution poststate root if N is empty.
